analysis:
This batch removes the retained console from repository tooling. It deletes the .githooks pre-commit and pre-push hooks and .github/dependabot.yml (npm for /console-ui). It drops the lint-console CI lane and its route entry from .github/workflows/ci.yml, and it edits one policy paragraph in .agents/skills/darkbloom-contributor/SKILL.md. None of it touches provider runtime code, the coordinator-provider WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), attestation (TB-009), the fan helper (TB-010), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), or the prefix cache (T-041, TB-007). Consumer data, keys and tokens are not handled by any changed file.

Checks I made. The provider-test-gate, release-integrity, docs and provider lanes are unchanged. No remaining job depends on lint-console via `needs`, as far as the supplied ci.yml shows. The route lane list still matches the remaining jobs. The `changes` workflow may still emit a `console` output, and it may reference console-ui paths; that is harmless, but component-changes.yml and branch-protection required-check names were not supplied. If branch protection requires the 'Console UI Lint & Build' check, merges would block, which is an availability issue and not a security regression.

Removed dependabot config: it had open-pull-requests-limit 0 and was scoped to /console-ui, so it only produced security-update PRs for npm. If console-ui/ files are still in the tree after this PR, they would lose automated security-update PRs and CI linting. That is a supply-chain hygiene gap for out-of-scope code; the threat model lists the console as out of scope. The SKILL.md change removes the statement that the console snapshot is retained, so it is consistent with the removal. Whether console-ui/ and its hosting config are actually deleted elsewhere in the PR is outside the supplied evidence. Integration should confirm that no deployed console-ui artifact remains without CI or dependency monitoring.
